title: One apparatus, two descriptions
question: Why should changing the observer change the explanation?
recap: Move the magnet past a resting conductor, or the conductor past a resting magnet: the current is the same, yet the physics of 1905 explained the two cases differently. Einstein's paper begins from that asymmetry and asks for one description that depends only on the relative motion.
premises: Both descriptions concern the same apparatus and the same events, seen from two inertial frames.
The principle of relativity and the constancy of the speed of light are assumptions, and stated as such.
limitations: A simulation built on the postulates cannot prove them.
The model of a magnet and a conductor loop does not cover every induction experiment.

overview.text: Move the magnet past a resting conductor, or the conductor past a resting magnet: the current is the same, yet the physics of 1905 explained the two cases differently. Einstein’s paper begins from that asymmetry and asks for one description that depends only on the relative motion.

full.text: In the usual account of 1905, a magnet moving past a conductor at rest creates an electric field, and that field drives the current. A conductor moving past a magnet at rest meets no electric field at all; the charges moving with it feel a force from the magnetic field instead, and that force drives the current. The two accounts predict the same current for the same relative motion. The paper sets out to remove the asymmetry of the explanation, not to show that the two observers measure the same fields: they do not.

Einstein raises two conjectures to the status of postulates. First, the laws of electrodynamics and optics hold in the same form in every frame in which the laws of mechanics hold. Second, light in empty space always travels with a definite speed \(V\), whatever the motion of the body that emits it. The paper takes them as its starting point; the unsuccessful attempts to detect motion relative to the ether are cited as what suggests the first, not as a proof of it.

The magnet-and-conductor laboratory compares the two descriptions for the same relative motion. At low speed the electric force in one frame equals the magnetic force in the other; at higher speed they differ by the factor \(\gamma\) derived in §6, which is how a force across the motion changes between frames.

steps.text: Letters: the paper writes V for the speed of light in empty space; this explanation writes c. It calls the frame in which Newton's equations hold the stationary system, K from §3 on, and a system moving uniformly relative to it k. The factor this explanation writes γ is the paper's β, which first appears in §3.

items: The apparatus: a magnet and a conductor, a loop of wire, in motion relative to each other, with the current in the conductor as the thing observed.

The first case, as the physics of 1905 explained it: the magnet moves and the conductor rests. Around the moving magnet an electric field arises, carrying a definite energy, and where parts of the conductor are, that field drives a current.

The second case: the magnet rests and the conductor moves. No electric field arises around the magnet. In the conductor there is instead an electromotive force, to which no energy corresponds in itself, and it drives a current.
Compare the observations: for the same relative motion, the current has the same size and the same course in both cases. What is observed depends only on the relative motion of conductor and magnet.
Compare the explanations: one case has an electric field and the other has none. The asymmetry lies in the account, not in what is observed.

Worked low-speed case: the conductor moves at 10 metres per second across a magnetic field of 0.5 tesla. On a charge q carried with it the magnetic force is qvB, and per unit charge that is \(vB=10\times0.5=5\) volts per metre. In the conductor's own frame §6 gives an electric field of γ times vB, and at this speed γ − 1 is about \(v^2/(2c^2)=5.6\times10^{-16}\): no measurement could tell the two numbers apart.
At 0.6c they differ by the factor γ = 1.25. §6 derives it: a force across the motion changes between frames by that factor, so the two accounts describe one push.

The paper adds a second kind of evidence: the unsuccessful attempts to detect the earth's motion relative to the medium of light. Together these lead to the conjecture that absolute rest corresponds to no property of the phenomena, in electrodynamics as in mechanics, and that the same laws of electrodynamics and optics hold in every coordinate system in which the equations of mechanics hold, as had already been shown for quantities of the first order.
The first premise, the principle of relativity: the paper raises that conjecture to a premise. It is assumed, not proved from the examples.

The second premise: light in empty space always travels with a definite speed V, independent of the state of motion of the body that emits it. The paper says the two premises are only apparently incompatible.

What the two premises are said to give: a simple and consistent electrodynamics of moving bodies, built on Maxwell's theory for bodies at rest. A light ether becomes superfluous, since no absolutely stationary space is introduced and no velocity is assigned to a point of empty space in which electromagnetic processes take place.

Where the work starts: every such theory rests on the kinematics of rigid bodies, since its statements concern rigid bodies used as coordinate systems, clocks, and electromagnetic processes. So §1 begins with what time means.
The status of the laboratory: a simulation built on the two premises shows their consequences. It cannot prove them.

margin.text: This page reconstructs the argument in modern words; it is not a translation of the paper’s opening. Whether the Michelson–Morley experiment shaped Einstein’s own route is a historical question with its own evidence; the paper itself cites only the unsuccessful attempts to detect the earth’s motion through the ether.
